facts.text: Paul Naschy flew to Hollywood for just one week in 2003 and shot this film plus Countess Dracula's Orgy of Blood back to back for director Fred Olen Ray.
The famous figure of 600+ victims for Countess Elizabeth Bathory is shaky: the highest count, 650, came from a servant's secondhand account of a courtier's claim about a book that was never found.
Biography.com says Countess Elizabeth Bathory's nickname, the Blood Countess, may have inspired Bram Stoker's Dracula. Guinness still lists her as the most prolific female murderer.
Paul Naschy, playing werewolf Waldemar Daninsky, never learned to speak English. That made shooting an American video production with a US crew a challenge.
In the companion film Countess Dracula's Orgy of Blood, Paul Naschy plays a priest, Padre Jacinto, who stakes two vampires in a 1897 prologue. Moria counts it as one of his few American roles.
Naschy brought his wife and son Sergio to the shoot. The day after they landed in LA, his wife was hospitalized with a stomach virus.
This is the 12th and last Waldemar Daninsky werewolf film, and the only one not written by Paul Naschy, who wrote most of his own horror movies.
Jay Richardson, who plays Richard Daninsky here, was the hero detective Jack Chandler in Hollywood Chainsaw Hookers (1988), a film that also starred this movie's Michelle Bauer.
Director Fred Olen Ray wrote the script himself but credited it to a pseudonym: Sherman Scott.
Cinematographer Gary Graver, who shot this movie, also directed and shot about 135 adult features under the name Robert McCallum, while shooting for Orson Welles for free.
Fred Olen Ray said in a later interview that this film never turned a profit, according to Troy Howarth's book Human Beasts: The Films of Paul Naschy.
The first Waldemar Daninsky film, 1968's Mark of the Wolf Man, was written by Paul Naschy, who didn't plan to star. He took the role when the producer couldn't find another actor.
It was shot on video, not film, in 2003. It went straight to VHS in an edited version in June 2004, then came out uncensored in 2015 as The Unliving.
Mark of the Wolf Man was released in the US as Frankenstein's Bloody Terror. Wikipedia says it was shot in 3-D and Hi-Fi 70mm but only shown in that format in Munich.
Gary Graver, this film's cinematographer, was handed Orson Welles' Citizen Kane Oscar as a keepsake after The Other Side of the Wind. He later sold it for $50,000, and Welles' daughter sued.
Cinematographer Gary Graver shot this film. In the early 1970s he had worked for low-budget horror filmmaker Al Adamson.
Director Fred Olen Ray made Bikini Airways in 2003 "on a lark and it did really well." It spawned a run of his softcore bikini films, including Bikini a Go-Go with this film's Beverly Lynne.
While in the US, Paul Naschy toured Universal Studios, home of the classic Wolf Man. He also visited the Ackermansion, the museum of Famous Monsters of Filmland editor Forrest J Ackerman.
Director Fred Olen Ray's first feature, The Brain Leeches (1978), cost $298. He co-wrote it with political essayist Brad Linaweaver.
Michelle Bauer's first lead role was in Fred Olen Ray's The Tomb (1986). She went on to play Countess Elizabeth Bathory for Ray here nearly 20 years later.
Michelle Bauer (Elizabeth Bathory) was Penthouse's Pet of the Month in July 1981. Her Penthouse work led to her audition for director Fred Olen Ray, who asked her to dye her hair black.
Ray's earlier The Tomb (1986) was made for about $185,000 and shot in roughly 13 days. It sold tens of thousands of videotapes, a lot for a direct-to-video title then.
Beverly Lynne (Leslie) starred in Fred Olen Ray's Bikini a Go-Go in 2004. Ray co-wrote it under the same pseudonym he used here, Sherman Scott.
Paul Naschy was a weightlifter and professional wrestler before acting. Director Fred Olen Ray also wrestled, as Fabulous Freddie Valentine.
Michelle Bauer's Hollywood Chainsaw Hookers (1988) cost between $60,000 and $95,000. In the UK, "Chainsaw" couldn't go in the title, so it was sold as Hollywood Hookers.
Paul Naschy's horror roles earned him the nickname the Spanish Lon Chaney. Spain gave him its Gold Medal of Merit in the Fine Arts in 2001.
Director Fred Olen Ray cast aging Buster Crabbe, star of three Flash Gordon serials, in his film Alien Dead. Ray also had a small role in Peter Cushing's Shock Waves (1975).
Fred Olen Ray once loaned a 16mm camera to Quentin Tarantino, who used it to make his early film My Best Friend's Birthday.
Michelle Bauer, Linnea Quigley and Brinke Stevens are the stars of the 2011 documentary Screaming in High Heels, which also interviews director Fred Olen Ray about the scream queen era.
Michelle Bauer has also been credited as Pia Snow and Kim Bittner. She has appeared in dozens of low-budget horror films.
Paul Naschy's 12 Waldemar Daninsky films set a werewolf record. Lon Chaney Jr. played Larry Talbot, the Wolf Man, in seven.
